# ws7-R3 span-confirm triage — unpinned candidate identity check (2026-07-02)

**Tool:** `tools/span_confirm.py` (oracle-plurality span-identity confirmer).
**Oracle:** `dc3_oracle.json` (33,987 rows, committed) — DC3↔RB3 function pairs.
**Splits:** `config/45410914/splits.txt` (1,078 pinned `.text` spans, 735 TUs at
this checkout).
**Generated by:** `python3 tools/span_confirm.py --calibrate` and
`--triage`. All numbers below are the tool's literal stdout — not hand-edited.

> **STANDING WARNING (printed by the tool):** NOT VALID for oracle-located
> candidates (ws3 dc3-cluster spans: `pin_candidates.json` / `game_splits.json`)
> — the oracle would vote for itself. Use only on spans located by an
> **independent** signal (ghidriff / BSim / crossval / contiguity).

## 1. Methodology + the circularity rule

MSVC `/O1` preserves per-TU spatial grouping in `.text` (no whole-program
reorder). So for a candidate `.text` span, the DC3-side TU (`dc3_tu`) of the
oracle rows whose `rb3_va` lands inside the span forms a **plurality vote** for
the span's true TU identity. Verdict per span:

- gather in-span oracle rows; let `top` = highest TU vote count, `second` = next.
- **ABSTAIN** if `n_rows < 5` (sparse) or `top < 3` (sparse-top) or
  `top < 2·second` (no-margin).
- else **CONFIRM** if the winning TU stem equals the claimed stem (with
  `ham`↔`band` twin normalization, e.g. `hamcamshot`≡`bandcamshot`), else
  **CONTRA**.

Name normalization strips path/`:`-prefixes and extension and lowercases, so the
oracle's `obj:Task.obj` → `task` pairs against a claim `Task.o` → `task`.

**Circularity rule (hard):** candidate spans are drawn ONLY from sources located
by an *independent* Wii↔Xenon signal (ghidriff ExactInstruction/BSim, BinDiff,
BSim crossval). Candidates from `pin_candidates.json` / `game_splits.json` are
**excluded** — those spans were *located by the dc3 oracle itself* (the ws3
pipeline), so confirming them with the same oracle is circular. This report does
not include them, by construction.

## 2. Calibration (honesty anchor — the acceptance gate)

Ground-truth eval on DC3-shared pinned TUs (truth = the `.cpp` basename; only
TUs whose stem exists in the oracle's TU set are scored). The committed tool
must clear **≥80% margin-gated precision at ≥50% coverage**; it does:

```
# span_confirm --calibrate  (DC3-shared pinned TUs, gate n>=5/top>=3/2x)
DC3-shared pinned TUs with >=1 in-span oracle row: 565
raw plurality accuracy:
  n>=5 : 206/284 = 72.5%
  n>=10: 135/202 = 66.8%
  n>=20: 87/142 = 61.3%
margin-gated (population = n>=5 TUs = 284):
  precision: 161/192 = 83.9%
  coverage : 192/284 = 67.6%
ACCEPTANCE (>=80% precision, >=50% coverage): PASS
```

The planner measured 132/158 = 84% at 158/250 = 63% on main @00c5b19; this
worktree (06938a5) has more pins, so the population grew to 284 (n≥5 TUs) and
the numbers land at **83.9% precision / 67.6% coverage** — the same regime, gate
**PASS**. Raw plurality (no gate) is 72.5% at n≥5, i.e. the margin gate buys
~11 points of precision by trading ~32% coverage, exactly the audited tradeoff.

## 3. Candidate sources (all independent of the dc3 oracle)

| source | file | provenance | rows | unpinned rows fed to triage |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| ghidriff | `ghidriff_identities.json` | Wii↔Xenon ExactInstruction / BSim (run3) | 978 | **320** unpinned |
| crossval | `docs/decomp/gameid/crossval_agree.json` | BinDiff + BSim agree (stem-only) | 146 `agree_fns` | 65 unpinned (re-checked live; the stored `already_pinned` flag is stale — 93 flagged vs 65 actually outside current spans) |
| sysnet-worklist | `sysnet_port_worklist.json` | Wii↔Xenon BSim/ghidriff | 516 | 265 unpinned |
| band3-worklist | `band3_port_worklist.json` | Wii↔Xenon BSim/ghidriff | 232 | 10 unpinned |

**Candidate construction** (`span_confirm.py --triage`): for each source, drop
rows whose `rb3_addr` already lies inside a current `splits.txt` `.text` span
(re-checked live, not trusting stale flags), group the residue by TU stem
(`.o`/`.obj` stripped, lowercased), keep stems with **≥2** unpinned fns, split
each stem's sorted VAs at gaps > 64 KiB into clusters, and emit
`span = [min_va, max_va + 0x400)` per cluster. Claim = the stem. Tag: crossval
rows are **stem-only, ~80–86% empirical precision, network stems uncalibrated**
(per ws7 R4).

## 5. Reading the results / the Quazal caveat

The **CONTRA** rows are the actionable signal: the oracle says the span is a
*different, high-density* TU than the ghidriff/BSim label claims. E.g. ghidriff
labels `0x822e3788–0x822e3b88` as `vocaltrackdir`, but 8 of 9 in-span oracle
rows are `os:System_Xbox.obj` (`__unwind$` funclets) — a genuine mislabel worth
manual review, not an auto-reject. `chordshapegenerator @0x822cb0f0` (88 rows,
top `object`×23) and `scheduler @0x82a97ad8` (top `url`×5) are similar
strong-CONTRA flags.

The **ABSTAIN**-heavy Quazal network region (`0x82A40000–0x82B30000` — most of
the ghidriff/sysnet unpinned residue: `Session`, `Station`, `CallContext`,
`ObjDupProtocol`, `DuplicationSpace`, `WKHandle`, `Scheduler`, etc.) is the
**expected** outcome, not a tool failure: DC3 ships Quazal but the oracle's
pairing density there is low and diffuse. This is visible directly in the tables
— e.g. `sessionclock @0x82a40630` spans 232 rows yet the top TU (`synapse_dsp`)
gets only 8 (3.4%): the region is a low-confidence oracle desert, so the gate
correctly abstains rather than guessing. Report the observed in-span counts, do
not spin them.

## 6. Consumers (how to fuse this into other streams)

- **ws2 worklist-regen triage** and **ws5 case-B target selection** should call
  `span_confirm.py` as a **fused pre-filter** over their candidate spans:
  CONFIRM = independent second witness (oracle agrees with ghidriff/BSim);
  ABSTAIN = no oracle signal, fall back to the primary locator; **CONTRA = flag
  for manual review, NEVER auto-reject** (the label may be right and the oracle
  span-boundary wrong, or vice-versa).
- **Hard limits:** the confirmer is **never a sole gate** and is **never valid
  for ws3 oracle-located targets** (circular). It is one cheap witness among
  ghidriff/BSim/BinDiff/contiguity, best used to rank a manual-review queue.

## 7. Conclusion — R3 reopen verdict

**R3 reopen: LAND (not dead).** The margin-gated confirmer clears the kill bar
(83.9% precision / 67.6% coverage ≥ 80%/50%) with the audited gate family
(n≥5, top≥3, top≥2× second, ham/band normalization) — no gate was weakened. The
tool is committed and read-only; it produces {5 CONFIRM, 20 CONTRA, 131 ABSTAIN}
over 156 unpinned independent-source candidate spans. Value is concentrated in
the small-but-clean game-region CONFIRMs (`dir`, `task`, `ui`, `synth`) and the
CONTRA mislabel flags; the network region is honestly abstained. Fold into
ws2/ws5 as a pre-filter witness, never as a sole gate.
